ModMetaData.name: Jawa Patches (local)
ModMetaData.author: mandrake
ModMetaData.description:
Local content + compatibility patches for the "crashed Factory ship / Jawa stowaways" gravship campaign. Self-authored, kept minimal and defensive. Each PATCH is wrapped in PatchOperationConditional so a missing target (mod not loaded, def renamed in an update) is a silent no-op instead of a red error. LOAD THIS LAST in the mod order (RimSort), after every mod it touches.
Currently contains: - Defs/WeatherDefs/SWDesertWeather.xml — four hazard weathers (sandstorm, dry sandstorm, red fog, red foggy rain) extracted from "Star Wars - Biomes Addon" (Ferreira312, WS 2298926362). Pure XML, no assembly: the mod's custom C# overlay classes were swapped for the vanilla fog overlay while keeping all gameplay fields (accuracy/move/wind/lightning). Sandstorm cuts ranged accuracy to 0.25; dry sandstorm adds lightning-started fires; red fog / foggy rain reduce accuracy (and, for the rain, move speed). - Patches/AnimalBiomeDuplicates_Fix.xml — removes 3 duplicate (biome, animal) registrations that crash BiomeDef.CommonalityOfAnimal(). Armadillo x AridShrubland and Armadillo x Desert (Beasts of the Rim's animal-side wildBiomes duplicating Odyssey's biome-side wildAnimals), and Titan x TropicalSwamp (the Titans mod lists the biome twice in its own def). Left unfixed these kill Choose Wild Animal Spawns outright, make Giddy-Up skip its animal-biome cache, and abort Biome Compatibility Project inside RimWorld's post-load queue. Detected by Utils/animal_inventory.py; re-run it after mod updates. Nothing is lost in-game — the biome-side registration still spawns the animal. - Patches/BiomeAnimalDanglingRefs_Fix.xml — the null-key sibling of the above. Primordial Geysers injects animals into its biome guarded on the mod name only, and five of the named PawnKindDefs do not exist here (Vanilla Animals Expanded drops badger/moose/muskox/porcupine when Odyssey is active, via IfModNotActive in its LoadFolders.xml; AA_WaywardMobileAssembler was removed from Alpha Animals). Each leaves a BiomeAnimalRecord with a null animal, and BiomeDef.CommonalityOfAnimal then throws ArgumentNullException on the null key — which is what kept Choose Wild Animal Spawns dead. Removing them costs nothing: they spawn nothing, and the biome already lists vanilla Porcupine and Moose. These nodes are created by another mod's patch at runtime, so they do not exist on disk and offline validators report zero matches; that is expected, and it is why this mod must load after Primordial Geysers. - Patches/SWCPZoomerIcon_Fix.xml — kills the last red error in the load. Star Wars KotOR Resources and Materials ships an AssetBundle reference it never packaged, so SWCP_VATS_Zoomer's custom Graphic_Zoomer returns a null Material and vanilla BuildableDef.ResolveIcon throws a NullReferenceException every launch. Verified from IL that exactly one def is responsible, and that BuildableDef's PostLoad lambda skips ResolveIcon entirely when uiIconPath is non-empty — so adding uiIconPath (512blank, a texture the mod already ships) makes the NRE structurally unreachable without changing any runtime behaviour. Note this is hygiene, not a rescue: the post-load queue does NOT abort on a failed action, contrary to what our notes long claimed. The two "Failed to load bundle" lines will remain; only the exception goes. - Patches/HeadSetForFA_Revive.xml — Head Set For [NL] Facial Animation has been dying in its static constructor every launch. Verified from IL: FaceAdjustmentDef's constructor never initialises AgeBasedParams, and CheckSettingData walks that list for any race with life stages. A sweep of all 45,525 XML files in the load set found exactly one adjustment def that omits the field — BS_InsectoidHumanoid_FourArmed_FaceAdjustment, created at runtime by Facial Animation Compatability Project. Adding an empty list fixes it. NOTE this is hygiene, not the appearance fix: HeadSetForFA only does head size/offset tuning and never touches eye nodes or head types. - Patches/DroidFemaleTexture_Fix.xml — Outer Rim Droid Depot ships only male body textures. All 11 droid body folders were checked and none has a Naked_Female variant, so any droid generated female renders with no body at all. Forces fixedGender Male on the 7 affected PawnKindDefs, which routes generation to textures that exist. Chose this over hasGenders=false because that yields Gender.None, whose Naked_None path does not exist either and would break every droid instead of some. - Patches/JawaAppearance_Tuning.xml — three appearance decisions. (a) Biotech's Skin_InkBlack is actually (55,55,55) charcoal; set to true (0,0,0). Note this is a Core gene shared by 13 active xenotypes, not Jawa-only. (b) Removes Outland_GreaterGoblinoidHead from BTD_Jawa: that head's ART has arachnid eyes and fangs baked in, which drew underneath the yellow-eye gene and gave Jawa two sets of eyes plus a fanged mouth. Without it the face is plain and only the glowing eyes show, which is the canonical read. (c) Adds Outland_AllMale so Jawa spawn male-only this playthrough. - Patches/SWDesertWeather_Attach.xml — injects those weathers into hot/arid biomes (sandstorms) and volcanic/exotic biomes (red fog) via baseWeatherCommonalities. Conditional-wrapped per biome. Tune the commonality numbers there to taste. - Defs/QuestScriptDefs/Jawa_TheClaim.xml — "The Claim", the campaign's first authored quest. Something came down past the ridge; clan law says the wreck belongs to whoever plants a marker on it first, and someone else is already walking. It is an item-stash site on the ground layer, offered on the ordinary opportunity cadence, expiring after 10–18 days with no penalty and no goodwill loss — the only thing lost is the opportunity. The haul is fixed rather than rolled so the reward rule is guaranteed instead of hoped for: one advanced component (the one category a starting clan cannot make, needing advanced fabrication and a fabrication bench), eight industrial components and four steel slag chunks. Deliberately at the low end. No node class, field or defName in it is guessed — each was read off a shipping def (Core's Script_ItemStash and Script_BanditCamp, Royalty's Script_Intro_Deserter and Scripts_Permits) and the file cites the path and line for every one. DLC defs are named for PROVENANCE only and never depended on: everything the quest actually references ships in Core, so a DLC or mod update cannot orphan it. everAcceptableInSpace is set true, and that field gates ACCEPTANCE BY THE PLAYER, not site placement — proven twice, from Core's keyed string QuestNotSpace ("cannot accept in space") sitting inside the run of quest accept-requirement strings, and from Odyssey's six genuinely orbital site quests setting the field zero times while Core's ground-only trade request sets it true. Core's own item-stash quest omits it, which means vanilla's stash quest is silently unacceptable while the colony is aboard a ship; this is a gravship campaign, so ours sets it and the site still lands on the ground. The rival clan that beats you to the wreck is a STORY FACT — no FactionDef is authored or referenced by it, and it exists only to explain why there is a timer. - Defs/ThingDefs_Items/Jawa_ClaimRumour.xml — "salvage rumour", a one-use readable that hands the player The Claim on the spot rather than waiting for the storyteller to offer it. Three comps do the entire job: CompProperties_Usable, CompProperties_UseEffectDestroySelf and CompProperties_UseEffectGiveQuest. Those comps are mostly USED by Biotech defs but the classes live in Assembly-CSharp, so this needs no DLC and references no DLC def. The pattern is borrowed rather than invented — Space Tower's ST_TowerMap is a shipping example of exactly this three-comp readable, and it was read before this was written. Note that the defName is Jawa_ClaimRumour while the label is "salvage rumour": that mismatch is deliberate, because a defName is never shown to the player and renaming it would churn the quest reference and every save holding one for no player-facing gain. This ships as the bare object — tradeability None, no faction, no price. Where rumours come from is designed and is NOT built here: bought from the Hutt Cartel, who know where everything fell and will sell you anything, AND found in wreck loot, because a clan that cannot afford rumours must never simply stop receiving content. Both lanes, trader stock and loot tables, are one line each and are the next step, not this one. To see it now: Debug actions, Spawn thing, Jawa_ClaimRumour; then select a colonist and right-click the item to read it. - Defs/TerrainDefs/JawaSaltCrust.xml — adds Jawa_SaltCrust, a hard pale evaporite pan: flat, blinding, takes footprints like chalk, grows nothing, and is the firmest ground on the planet. It is COSMETIC ONLY and that is a design guardrail, not an omission — fertility 0, no yield, no comp, nothing farmable or harvestable, because farmable-anywhere or passive-resource terrain is an anti-exponential violation dressed as scenery. Salt as a trade good is a separate, later piece of work. The art is reused, not drawn: texturePath is Odyssey's own Terrain/Surfaces/DryLakeBed, which nothing in Core, any DLC or any biome def actually references — it ships unused, so this terrain adopts it rather than competing with it. The consequence worth knowing is that the texture lives in Odyssey's asset bundle, so the crust's appearance depends on Odyssey being active. <color> pushes the cracked hardpan toward evaporite white; if a future version stops honouring colour on natural terrain, DryLakeBed is still visually distinct from Sand and SoftSand, so this degrades to "less white" rather than to "invisible" — which is why it beat tinting Sand. ParentName is NaturalTerrainBase and NOT Sand on purpose: inheriting from Sand would also inherit its tools (kick material in eyes) and its sand filth, neither of which belongs on a mineral crust. Every remaining field was copied from a def read on disk, with the source file and line recorded per field. - Patches/JawaTerrain_SaltPans.xml — the attachment half of the above. A TerrainDef on its own generates NOWHERE, exactly as a WeatherDef on its own blows nowhere; a biome has to ask for it, and this file is that ask. It adds a terrain patch maker for Jawa_SaltCrust to the three CORE arid biomes — Desert, Extreme Desert and Arid Shrubland — tuned to read as one big lake bed rather than a speckle: perlin frequency below Core's, a minimum patch size roughly double Core's, and a fertility ceiling so pans only form on the driest ground. What the player sees is broad, pale, cracked salt pans lying in the low ground of desert maps, unmistakably not sand and flat enough to build and land on. Desert and Extreme Desert already own a terrainPatchMakers node so those are a plain conditional add; Arid Shrubland has no such node at all, so it is guarded on the CONTAINER and the nomatch branch creates the whole element — adding a child to a node that does not exist is the failure mode where one dead operation silently kills every operation after it in the same sequence. The sibling dune file guards Arid Shrubland identically, so whichever applies first creates the node and the other takes the match branch: order-independent by construction. One thing NOT to hunt: Geological Landforms Harmony-patches TerrainPatchMaker itself, and on a tile carrying a landform that landform's own graph can write terrain over the biome result. On ordinary tiles the pans generate normally. Geological Landforms' own dry-lake landform hard-codes soft sand and sand, so the one map feature that ought to be a salt pan is the one place this cannot reach. - Patches/JawaTerrain_DuneSeas.xml — turns the arid maps from a flat sheet of sand with occasional soft patches into a dune sea. It adds NO new def and NO new art: Core already ships one SoftSand patch maker per hot desert biome, and the only number touched is that threshold's lower bound — 0.65 down to 0.55 in Desert and to 0.50 in Extreme Desert, because the deep desert is the dune sea proper and is already 100 percent sand at every fertility. Lower threshold means more of the perlin field clears the bar, which means wider dunes; perlin output clusters around 0.5, so 0.65 is roughly the top sixth of a map and 0.55 roughly the top third. Arid Shrubland has no dunes at all today and gains one patch maker, kept off the fertile ground so the biome still reads as shrubland rather than as a second desert. This is the one terrain change with a gameplay cost rather than a purely visual one: SoftSand is path cost 14 against Sand's 4, so widening the dunes genuinely slows a crossing, and that is intended — the world is a desert sea to cross, not a place to settle. Those two numbers plus Arid Shrubland's are the entire tuning surface; raise them back toward 0.65 to undo. The replace operations select on the SoftSand threshold specifically, which is what keeps them order-independent against the salt-pan file adding a second entry to the same list. - Defs/MapGeneration/JawaScrapfields.xml plus Patches/JawaResource_Scrapfields.xml — the pair that strews the desert with wreckage. The first declares a GenStepDef that scatters steel slag chunks with machine-bit filth trodden around them; the second registers it into the player map generator, because a GenStepDef that no MapGeneratorDef lists runs on no map at all. What the player sees is slag lying half-buried across the open desert — not in ruins, not in a mountain, out where you land — so the planet reads as somewhere things have been crashing for a very long time, which is the reason a clan of scavengers is standing on it. Slag was chosen because it is the cheapest possible thing to strew: it smelts to 15 steel and only after a smelter, power and hauling, so a littered map is atmosphere with a work cost attached rather than free loot. Raising the vanilla junk-cluster density instead would have handed out sealed crates of finished gear, which is an arms race this campaign does not want. Every field on the gen step is copied from a shipping GenStep_ScatterThings; clusterSize and spotMustBeStandable were deliberately left out because they appear on no shipped def of that class anywhere, and a field the engine does not read is a silent no-op at best. The one number worth arguing about is the count: 12–20 per 10,000 cells puts roughly 75 to 125 chunks on a 250x250 map, two or three visible per screen, which is the density that makes the world READ as junk-strewn — Core's own debris step runs 0.25–0.5, one or two per map. Full theoretical yield if every chunk were smelted is about 1,100 to 1,900 steel per map, one-off and non-renewing. It is registered against the player-settlement generator ONLY, deliberately, so encounter maps, faction bases and quest maps are untouched; one more operation aimed at the abstract common generator widens it to the whole planet. - Patches/JawaCombatViability_Tuning.xml — the attachment half of the above: it swaps Turn_Gene_Terrified for RimMandrake_Jawa_Skittish on BTD_Jawa. A Jawa fainted mid-firefight during the ion blaster acceptance test, and that is the gene working exactly as its author designed it — canon Jawa are famously cowardly. The problem is purely that OUR COLONISTS ARE ALL JAWA, and a colony that faints when attacked cannot defend the gravship. ⚠️ It would have got worse, not better: fainting frequency scales with surrounding Terror, the gene multiplies Terror by 1.5, and Terror comes from corpses, prisoners and slaves — this is a slaver campaign, so the exact conditions the campaign is built around are the ones that make it fire most often. It would have read as a difficulty curve rather than as a gene. The donor gene is left completely untouched, because it is also carried by guy762_xenotype_nemoidian and BTD_Neimoidian, who are NPC-only and whose fainting costs the player nothing. - Defs/PawnKindDefs/AlienSpawnEnablers.xml — 13 dev-spawn pawnkinds for Star Wars species that no pawnkind could otherwise reach. Debug "Spawn Pawn" lists PawnKindDefs, not xenotypes, and of the 74 species with a xenotype only 43 were reachable; the other 31 were fully-authored xenotypes nothing in the game could ever instantiate. Only species that are genuinely READY are added — head gene present AND that head's art present. ⚠️ Readiness is deliberately NOT a file-existence test: vanilla art is packed into Unity bundles (Core ships two loose PNGs and no Textures folder at all), and Outer Rim Galactic Diversity keeps its 554 head PNGs under a Common_Old folder its own LoadFolders.xml never lists, yet they render. A naive test gives false negatives in both directions and would have neutralised dozens of working heads, so readiness here means the art is either directly on disk under a loaded Textures path or sits in the same Outer Rim Heads folder as Bith and Mon Calamari, both confirmed rendering. Copied verbatim from Outer Rim's own OuterRim_MonCalamari pawnkind and pointed at the BTD_ xenotypes on purpose, because REMIX remaps 88 pawnkinds at runtime and BTD_ is the side that survives. Known compromises, upstream's choice not ours: Lasat and Zygerrian reuse the Cathar head, Muun the Quarren, Ortolan the Kubaz, Nelvaanian the Bothan. The two Sith entries are here only because they are technically ready — given the campaign's Force rules they are the likeliest to be unwanted, and deleting those two defs is the whole removal. - Defs/XenotypeDefs/GamorreanXenotype.xml — a custom Gamorrean, forked from guy762_xenotype_gamorrean rather than derived from vanilla Pigskin, because the two Star Wars Gamorreans already in the load set are purpose-built for the setting and Pigskin is not. 23 of the donor's 24 genes are inherited verbatim and every one was confirmed present in the live DefDump before this was written; none is guessed. Two deliberate changes: Ears_Pig is ADDED, the single biggest appearance win available with zero new art, because vanilla Biotech ships drooping pig ears as an overlay gene that neither existing Gamorrean uses and they widen the silhouette in exactly the south and north views where the species currently reads as a bald human; and Headbone_MiniHorns is REMOVED, because Gamorreans have tusks, not horns, and composited against the real head art the mini-horns read as devil horns. That second one is a taste call — re-add the single line to restore upstream exactly. ⚠️ Open question, deliberately not resolved here: the scale atlas puts the Gamorrean at 1.3–1.6 m, SHORTER than the human standard, while the inherited guy762_BodySizeGene_big says the opposite. Body size feeds combatPower, melee reach and carrying capacity, so shrinking the Hutts' door-muscle is a campaign decision and not a cleanup. And what this does NOT fix is the head: there is no species head gene for either Gamorrean in any of the three xenotype mods (verified against the live GeneDef dump, not inferred), so a Gamorrean wears a vanilla heavy-jaw human skull with a flat pig-nose decal. That gap is what commissioned art fills. - Defs/PawnKindDefs/GamorreanPawnKinds.xml — two pawnkinds, a guard and a heavier one, that make the above xenotype a thing which can actually stand in the world. Before this file all 1718 PawnKindDefs in the live dump were searched and ZERO mentioned Gamorrean; the species existed only as an entry in the pawn-editor list. The find that made it worth doing: the KotOR mods already ship a complete canon Gamorrean kit that nothing equips — the Arg'garok axe, the Kajidic Soldier's Axe, a vibroaxe and vibroglaive, Gamorrean leathers, a leather hood and the M'uhk'gfa heavy armour, with per-body-type art including Fat, the body the xenotype uses. Every def and texture was confirmed on disk. The weapons even carry an "HC_" (Hutt Cartel) tag prefix, so the upstream author plainly intended Hutt Cartel pawnkinds and never shipped them. Standalone defs with no ParentName, deliberately: OuterRimTestColonyPawnKind hard-sets defaultFactionDef to PlayerColony, which is right for a dev-spawn stub and wrong for a hostile species. ⚠️ THESE DO NOT RAID YOU. A pawnkind only enters world generation when a faction lists it in pawnGroupMakers, and this file patches no faction on purpose. There is no Hutt Cartel faction at all — all 81 loaded factions were checked and none matches hutt, cartel, crime, pyke, slaver or black-sun — so defaultFactionDef points at OuterRim_BinaryStarRaiders, the closest thing the stack has to Hutt muscle. Until a Cartel exists these are reachable through dev mode, which is exactly enough to look at the species and judge the art. - Patches/HuttEyes_Slitted.xml — re-points BTD_Hutt's eye colour from the four stock guy762_Eyes_Big* genes to six warm vertical-slit genes from [LFS] Genes Expanded - Eyes. Hutts were spawning with the same huge round glowing eyes as the Jawa, which is right for a Jawa and wrong for a Hutt. This introduces no new mechanism: all of them are children of the abstract GeneEyeColor whose exclusionTags are [EyeColor], so the engine already picks exactly one per pawn — proven on our own Jawa the same day, 31 pawns came out 16 amber / 8 orange / 7 yellow from three listed genes. Green is deliberately dropped; BTD_Hutt carries seven skin genes and all of them are some shade of green, and green eyes on green skin was part of why the face read flat. The REPTILE family is what ships, not the feline one the header first chose — that was retargeted on the owner's call after seeing the feline eyes on screen. Wrapped in PatchOperationFindMod so the whole file is a silent no-op if the LFS mod is removed, and the removals sit INSIDE that same guard on purpose: dropping the stock four without the replacements available would leave Hutts with no eye gene at all. - Patches/HuttEyes_RestoreRenderNodes.xml — the other half of that change, and it must move with it. Hutts came out with "little black eyelashed eyes" rather than slits, and the live dump showed why: [LFS] Genes Expanded - Eyes ships an FA-compatibility patch that does PatchOperationRemove on renderNodeProperties for every one of its eye genes, gated on Facial Animation being INSTALLED rather than on the pawn being FA-driven. Its reasoning is sound for its own use case — if FA paints the face, the gene's eye art would double-draw. But BTD_Hutt is deliberately EXCLUDED from FA so the slit art can show, so neither party drew an eye and what remained was the head texture's own baked-in eyelashes. This puts the render nodes back on just the genes BTD_Hutt uses, copied verbatim from the donor's own definitions. ⚠️ BOTH the reptile and the legacy feline family are restored, on purpose: the xenotype rolls Reptile for new pawns while already-generated pawns keep Feline in their saved data and would otherwise go eyeless. drawSize is the one deliberate deviation from the donor's 0.21, and it is SETTLED at 0.30 by the owner on 2026-08-13 after being seen on screen — do not walk the ladder, every rung that used to be recorded here is above the shipped value. What the four failed iterations taught: the lever on eye separation is drawSize alone, because horizontal position comes from the head's own RightEye/LeftEye anchorTags; a quarter-eye gap does not read as two eyes, because each iris carries a dark slit about as wide as the gap and the two dark outlines touch, enclosing both irises in one capsule; and a measurement can confirm a number and still miss the read. The real fix is art, not a number — a narrower, taller eye keeps apparent size while opening a horizontal gap. - Patches/WookieeHead_Upgrade.xml — swaps guy762_Head_wookiee for OuterRim_WookieeHead on BTD_Wookiee, so Wookiees use Outer Rim's 512x512 head art instead of Star Wars Xenotypes' 128x128. Verified against the live DefDump: two complete Wookiee head chains exist and NEITHER IS BUGGY — both are properly gated with requiredGenes, so neither pollutes the open head pool, and the difference is purely which art they point at. The Wookiee is the single outlier in the Star Wars Xenotypes pack, which ships every other species at 512x512. REMIX picked the lower-resolution one knowingly: its own XenotypeEquivalencies.xml names all three Wookiee xenotypes as one species group, so this is a judgement call by its author and not a defect, which is exactly why a local patch is the right remedy rather than a bug report. The trade-off is accepted: Star Wars Xenotypes ships three head variants and Outer Rim ships one, so after this every Wookiee shares a head — at 128 px the three were barely distinguishable and 4x linear resolution is the larger win. No body art is missing, contrary to an earlier audit that looked for a BodyType/wookiee folder and read absence as absence: Furskin is a Biotech gene whose renderNodeProperties attach a fur node to the Body tag, so the fur IS the body treatment, and BTD_Wookiee already carries it. - Patches/SpeciesStartingGear_Tuning.xml — puts the Jawa in a hood and robes and the Hutts in nothing. Every Star Wars species spawned through Outer Rim's test-colony pawnkind was arriving dressed as a modern civilian, most of them in a surgical face mask: counted off a save, 54 of 76 Jawa, 13 of 16 Hutt and 7 of 11 Gungan wore Apparel_ClothMask, plus jeans, tank tops and aprons. ⚠️ The pawnkind cannot stop it, and that is the interesting part. OuterRimTestColonyPawnKind already asks for exactly the right thing and is being ignored — apparelTags is IndustrialBasic, apparelAllowHeadgearChance is 0 so headgear should be impossible, and headgear is fitted anyway; meanwhile vanilla Apparel_ClothMask declares no apparel tags at all and no active mod patches any onto it, so under stock rules it is not reachable through apparelTags in the first place. Something in the stack is bypassing pawnkind apparel generation wholesale; twelve active assemblies reference PawnApparelGenerator and Faction Loadout is the standout suspect, NOT confirmed. So rather than fight for control of the generator this uses the one channel that does not go through it: apparelRequired is applied directly to the pawn, and apparelMoney 0 leaves the generator no budget to bolt jeans and a mask on top. Both halves are needed — apparelRequired alone still lets the random pass add the mask, apparelMoney 0 alone leaves a naked Jawa. The art already exists: KotOR Core ships guy762_JawaHood and guy762_Robes_jawa, whose coverage does not overlap so both can be worn together. Hutts wear nothing DELIBERATELY — there is no Hutt garment anywhere in the load set, the two "hutt" apparel defs are the guards' armour rather than the boss's clothing, and canonically a Hutt wears nothing. Scoped to Jawa and Hutt only: for the other eleven species from AlienSpawnEnablers.xml apparelMoney 0 would mean naked, and there is no researched outfit to require yet. If a mask still appears after this, apparelMoney 0 was overridden too and the fix moves out of XML into Faction Loadout's config. - Patches/IonStunMote_Blue.xml — tints vanilla's Mote_Stun pale blue, the Jawa ion signature. The arcing electricity over a stunned pawn is Core's Mote_Stun and its graphicData declares NO colour, so it draws untinted white; adding one is the whole change, and the texture, timing, altitude layer and thingClass all stay vanilla's. The hue is deliberately the same one JawaIon_Damage already uses for its explosion edge, so a bolt's impact flash and the stun arc it leaves behind read as one effect rather than two. ⚠️ THIS IS GLOBAL, and that is a choice, not an oversight: RimWorld spawns the mote from StunHandler against a hardcoded ThingDefOf.Mote_Stun, so there is no XML route to a per-source colour. Accepted knowingly — KotOR stun bolts, Outer Rim stun grenades and sonic weapons also arc pale blue, which is consistent for energy weapons; the one odd fit is the Gamorrean Arg'garok, an axe whose edge tool carries ExtraDamage Stun at chance 1.0. Living with it, because "electric shock looks like this here" is a coherent rule and a per-weapon exception is not worth C# for a tint. Written as a Conditional rather than a plain Add so it cannot duplicate the node if Ludeon ever adds one. - Patches/GalacticEmpire.xml — reskins vanilla `Empire` (Royalty) into the Galactic Empire, the sector occupier. (Renamed 2026-08-20, when the owner struck the differently-named sector occupier this file used to build; the Empire has no name but the Galactic Empire. The Outer Rim FACTION def is no longer touched; its Imp* PAWN KINDS still are.) Label-level only: name, leader title, colour. ⚠️ fixedName is patched and not just label, and that is the trap this file exists to avoid — label is the def's display label, fixedName is the name the world object actually carries, and the shipped def sets BOTH to "Galactic Empire". Patch only label and the faction still introduces itself as the Galactic Empire on the world map, the comms console and the faction list; the acceptance gate is "the faction is SEEN on the world map", so fixedName is the field the gate actually reads, and missing it would produce a reskin that passes a file diff and fails the gate. The colour is CHOSEN, not specified, and is one value to change if the owner disagrees: shipped is pure white, canonically Imperial but near-invisible as a world-map marker on a pale desert planet, so this is a cold steel grey instead. Everything mechanical is deliberately untouched — no goodwill, no settlement counts, no pawnGroupMakers, no memes, no techLevel — because the scarce resource is verification passes, not authoring. One genuine discrepancy was found while reading and filed rather than fixed: the shipped def has permanentEnemy false while the faction dossier says permanent enemy yes. That is a mechanical field, so it is recorded elsewhere and NOT quietly changed inside a label-only patch. - Patches/RebelAlliance_Suppress.xml — keeps Outer Rim - Rebel Alliance enabled for its content while keeping the FACTION off the world map. This is a suppression, not a removal, and success is a negative observation: no Rebel Alliance settlement anywhere, AND OuterRim_A280Blaster still resolvable. Read from disk with the game down: the faction def carries requiredCountAtGameStart 1, and that is the field that matters — it does not merely make the faction likely, it makes it MANDATORY, because RimWorld forces the count at world generation and also tops up missing required factions when an existing save is loaded. Enabling the mod without this would therefore plant the faction whether or not a new world is rolled; settlementGenerationWeight 0.3 then keeps placing bases and canMakeRandomly true lets more appear later. All four fields are literally present in the child def rather than inherited, so all four ops are plain Replaces. The def is deliberately NOT deleted: the same mod's Scenario_Rebel.xml references it by name, so deleting it would trade a world-map annoyance for a "Could not resolve cross-reference" red error on every launch. Nothing here touches a ThingDef, so the A280, its bullet and all Rebel gear stay resolvable, and the pawnkinds are untouched — Rebel troopers can still arrive however events spawn them, they simply have no territory. ⚠️ SCOPE: this is world-GENERATION suppression and does not retroactively delete a Rebel Alliance that a save has already generated. maxConfigurableAtWorldCreation 0 also removes the faction from the world-creation picker so it cannot be re-added by accident; to opt back in, revert that one op rather than the whole file.
⚠️ TEXTURES: this mod ships exactly ONE, and it belongs to a def in this mod — Textures/Things/Item/Special/JawaClaimRumour.png, the salvage rumour's item art. It used to also carry three loose overrides repairing typo'd filenames in Vanilla Gravship Expanded and VRE Saurid; those now ship in GravshipAstronautFix and SauridFrillFix, one fix mod per donor mod. Do not re-add them: two loose files at one texture path are resolved by load order rather than by intent, and a texture that loses to another texture produces no log line at all.
⚠️ The two terrain patches and the scrapfields scatter all act at MAP GENERATION TIME. None of them changes a map that already exists — the salt pans, the wider dunes and the slag fields appear on newly generated maps only.
